en: The Fourteenth Chapter on the Alphabet from the *Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā-sūtra*.
[Posthumous titles: Kaifu Yitong Sisi, Teshen, Shih Hongluqing, Duke of Susuo;
with a fief of three thousand households; conferred the purple robe and the title of Sikong; posthumously titled Dajian, with the formal name Da Guang.
*Jñāna*: Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple, in accordance with the Imperial Decree. At that time, Mañjuśrī addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"How is it that all dharmas enter into these letter-syllables and the syllables of the dhāraṇī?
The Buddha told Mañjuśrī:
"All dharmas enter into the letter-syllables and the syllables of the dhāraṇī."
Mañjuśrī! For example:
"When the letter 'A' (ā) is pronounced, it is the sound of impermanence."
"When pronouncing the syllable *ā* (long), it is the sound of being far removed from the self.
When pronouncing the syllable *ī* (high-pitched), it is the sound of the vastness of the sense faculties.
When pronouncing the syllable *ī* (long), it is the sound of calamities in the world."
"When pronouncing the syllable *ūṃ*, it is the sound of various forms of oppression.
When pronouncing the syllable *uḥ*, it is the sound of the diminution of many sentient beings in the world."
"When pronouncing the syllable *jña*, it is the sound of sentient beings who are upright, gentle, and continuous.
When pronouncing the extended and departing sound *jñāḥ*, it is the sound of those who have severed defilements and sport in liberation."
"When pronouncing the syllable *ra*, it is the sound of the characteristic of arising phenomena (*utpāda-dharma-lakṣaṇa*).
When pronouncing the syllable *laṃ* (with the vowel *ā*), it is the sound of the characteristic of defilement within the three realms of existence (*traidhātuka-saṃkleśa-lakṣaṇa*).
When pronouncing the syllable *ya*, it is the sound of giving rise to that which is sought."
When pronouncing the syllable *ai*, it is the sound of superior deportment.
When pronouncing the syllable *u*, it is the sound of grasping.
When pronouncing the syllable *au*, it is the sound of miraculous birth.
"When pronouncing the syllable 'aṃ', it is the sound of 'non-self' (anātman).
When pronouncing the syllable 'aḥ', it is the sound of 'sinking.
When pronouncing the syllable 'ka', it is the sound of 'entering into the maturation of karma.'"
"When pronouncing the syllable Kha, there arises the sound of all dharmas being equal to space.
When pronouncing the syllable Ga, there arises the sound of the profound Dharma."
"When pronouncing the syllable *ga*, it is the sound that destroys density, ignorance, and darkness.
When pronouncing the syllable *ya*, it is the sound of the purification of the five destinies."
"When pronouncing the syllable *ja*, it is the sound of the Four Noble Truths.
When pronouncing the syllable *ca* (with the high tone), it is the sound of non-concealment of desire.
When pronouncing the syllable *jha*, it is the sound of transcending old age and death."
When pronouncing the character "Zan" (pronounced *zài* with the initial *gě*), it is the sound that subdues evil speech.
When pronouncing the character "Niáng" (upper tone), it is the sound that subdues the Māras of others.
"When pronouncing the syllable *ṭha*, it is the sound of cutting off speech.
When pronouncing the syllable *ṭha*, it is the sound of giving a definitive answer.
When pronouncing the syllable *ṇa*, it is the sound of subduing the disputes of Māra."
"When pronouncing the syllable *ca*, it is the sound of the realm of extinguishing defilements.
When pronouncing the nasalized syllable *ṇa*, it is the sound of eliminating all afflictions."
"When pronouncing the letter *ta* with the *udātta* accent, it is the sound of the uninterrupted continuity of *tathatā*.
When pronouncing the letter *tha* with the *udātta* accent, it is the sound of courageous progress through power."
"When pronouncing the syllable Na, it is the sound of the discipline of subduing, of tranquility, and of peace.
When pronouncing the syllable Dha, it is the sound of the seven noble riches."
"When pronouncing the syllable *na*, it is the sound of universally knowing name-and-form (*nāmarūpa*).
When pronouncing the syllable *pa*, it is the sound of the ultimate truth (*paramārtha*).
When pronouncing the syllable *pha*, it is the sound of attaining and realizing the fruit."
"When pronouncing the syllable *ma*, it is the sound of liberation from bondage.
When pronouncing the syllable *ba*, it is the sound of birth within the three realms of existence (*trai-dhātuka*).
When pronouncing the nasalized sound *maṅ* and the syllable *hu*, it is the sound of quelling pride."
"When pronouncing the syllable *ya*, it is the sound of the Buddha’s universal penetration.
When pronouncing the syllable *ra* (pronounced with the *li-ja* [zhǎ] tone), it is the sound of the ultimate meaning of pleasure and non-pleasure.
When pronouncing the syllable *la*, it is the sound of severing the branches of craving."
"When pronouncing the syllable *vaṃ*, it is the sound of the Supreme Vehicle (*anuttarayāna*).
When pronouncing the syllable *śa*, it is the sound of the emergence of faith, diligence, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom."
"When pronouncing the syllable *sa*, it is the sound of the wisdom that subdues the six sense bases and attains the six supernormal powers (*ṣaḍabhijñā*).
When pronouncing the syllable *sa* (with the *udātta* accent), it is the sound of the direct realization of all-knowledge (*sarvajñatā*)."
"When pronouncing the syllable *kha*, it is the sound of destroying afflictions and being free from desire.
When pronouncing the syllable *gi* (pronounced as a conjunct), it is the sound of the ultimate ineffability of all letters."
"Mañjuśrī! This is called the meaning of the syllables; all syllables enter into this.
— From the "Chapter on Syllables" of the *Mañjuśrīparipṛcchā-sūtra*.
